diagram_math_checks.evidence: Refutation 1.1 fixes A={0,1} in Set with cartesian tensor (Fact L2). Each displayed arrow has domain and codomain A. The top edge is c:A→A, c(a)=0; the left, right and bottom edges are 1_A:A→A.
Both horizontal arrows point right and both vertical arrows point down. The top/right route is 1_A∘c=c. The left/bottom route is 1_A∘1_A=1_A, exactly Refutation 2.1.
The two morphisms are unequal because c(1)=0 whereas 1_A(1)=1, with 0≠1 in A. No commutativity mark or equality of routes is asserted; the caption explicitly denies commutativity.

Fact L1 and its local remark supplier restrict coherence to formal canonical morphisms between parenthesisations of one ordered tensor word. The canonical-morphism definition permits structural associators/unitors, inverses, identities, tensoring and composition; it does not turn the arbitrary noninvertible constant map c into a structural map. The caption preserves that scope.
